newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: PORTUGUESE SHARES SHARPLY UP, OPTIMISM CONTINUES.
newsitem.headline: PORTUGUESE SHARES SHARPLY UP, OPTIMISM CONTINUES.

text.p: Portuguese shares ended sharply higher as optimism continued, with 10 blue chips hitting new highs, led by the banking sector. A recommendation of Banco Portugues de Investimento on banking stocks sent most banks to new highs. Turnover on Lisbon bourse was 23 billion escudos.

* Inparsa, despite a planned capital increase, construction group Engil-SGPS, electrical engineering group Efacec, Mundial Confianca and several banks, excluding BESC, hit all-time highs. Portugal Telecom ended at a session high of 7,580 escudos, up 130, after the cabinet approved a law authorising the third stage privatisation of 26 percent of the capital of Portugal's dominant telecommunications operator.

* Dealers said the market could rise again tomorrow as optimism prevailed about the robust performance of the economy, the climate of falling interest rates and expectations of strong company results. Foreign investors had returned to the market, encouraged by its prospects, they added.
* "There is a lot of liquidity in the market and optimism prevails. Tomorrow we'll see more rises, but perhaps with less force than today," oen dealer said.
* An analyst said: "Portugal is becoming a very attractive market for both domestic and foreign investors and if firms continue to show good results, the trend is just one way -- upwards."
He added: "There are some investors who consider that Portugal is still cheap."
